Resolves #20548

`Effort.md` is a Benefits page, and its advantage section opened with a cost: "a slightly higher initial learning curve or setup effort". It now leads with where the chart above it shows Neo's curve winning: below vanilla JavaScript by the time a website becomes a simple web application, and below a typical framework before that application turns complex.

The section states setup as one command, keeps the operator's "within about a week", and names a coding agent's native fluency with JSON blueprints. "Other frameworks" in `Effort.md` and `Speed.md` no longer files Neo under frameworks.

Evidence: L1 (docs-only: relative links, whitespace, a shelf-phrase grep with a positive control) → L1 required (AC-1 to AC-3). No residuals.

## AC Evidence
| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | `Effort.md:13-17` leads with the curve crossings as the chart draws them (`ComplexityAndEffort.png`, the operator's). It names `npx neo-app@latest` as the one-command setup (`README.md` Quickstart), keeps "within about a week", and links `JSONFirstUIs.md`. "Upfront investment" and "quickly recouped" are gone |
| AC-2 | `git grep -n -i -E 'other (javascript )?frameworks' -- learn/benefits/body/Effort.md learn/benefits/body/Speed.md` exits 1 (no match). The positive control, the same grep on `origin/dev`, matches 2 lines (`Effort.md:19`, `Speed.md:7`) |
| AC-3 | `check-relative-links.mjs`: OK. `check-whitespace.mjs`: exit 0 |
